name: Ameenji Rubber Limited
identity_note: Legal name and security checked in cited issuer/exchange filing.
summary:
Ameenji is a real engineered-rubber manufacturer with documented railway orders, but growth is not translating into dependable shareholder cash. FY 26 revenue rose 31.04% to ₹123.2499 crore while statutory PAT fell to ₹6.3393 crore and CFO fell to about ₹1.6407 crore. The latest half-year is especially important: H 2 revenue was ₹80.5458 crore, but core EBITDA margin was only about 10.04% and PAT ₹1.9634 crore. A full-year margin alone obscures that deterioration.

At the 19 October 2026 secondary close of ₹247.05, the financed base model produces approximately ₹210.99 terminal value and −3.11% annual return over five years. It assumes partial margin recovery to 13%, not continuation of the exceptionally strong H 1. Bull value is approximately ₹617.20, but requires sustained higher growth, 17% margins and better working-capital efficiency. Bear value is about ₹10.95 and severe stress wipes out modeled equity. These are conditional estimates, not price targets with assured realization.

BQS 4.86, Growth Quality GQS 5.00 after the persistent-cash-conversion cap, and IAS 2.465 support an unattractive-at-this-price classification rather than a compounder claim. No trade is recommended for a personal portfolio. The ₹5 lakh implementation test is only a reference and is constrained by a ₹2.9646 lakh trading lot and one-price declining sessions.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Identity: Ameenji Rubber Limited, ISIN INE 14 QA 01016, BSE code 544555, BSE SME. The audited annual report states listing/trading approval effective 6 October 2025. Issued shares are 11,280,000 and face value ₹10; the official interoperability master agrees and shows a 1,200-share lot. Its BSE-listed indicator must not be mistaken for an NSE primary listing, and a normal-market eligibility flag alone is not a trading prohibition. Cutoff is 20 October 2026; quote date is 19 October. No undated intake price is used as current evidence.

G 1 is Conditional: historical compliance disclosures and related dealings require monitoring, without a misconduct finding. G 2 is Conditional at Medium evidence confidence: signed audited aggregate statements, detailed notes and an explicit IPO restatement bridge support the model. Different statutory/restated PAT series are not silently mixed. G 3 is Conditional: the model funds authorized IPO spending once, includes licence costs and debt repayments, and exposes equity requirements rather than assuming the ₹450 crore authority creates cash. G 4 is Conditional: complete secondary daily observations support a bounded implementation estimate, but no current live order book or comprehensive BSE surveillance clearance is established.

The US subsidiary is 90% owned, subscribed on 21 June 2024, with no revenue or PAT in the annual AOC 1. Its tiny reported capital/net assets do not justify a US growth premium. Forecast uncertainty is separate from Medium confidence in reviewed historical amounts. Older FY 21–22 accounts are statutory and merger-affected; the scored revenue window is the post-amalgamation FY 23–26 series.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors are GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV 7, DUR 6, CAP 4, CASH 3, BAL 3, EXEC 5, EARN 4, R 1, D 2, P 2 and L 3. Every factor has a source-linked audit object. BQS = 0.20×5 + 0.20×5 + 0.12×7 + 0.10×6 + 0.12×4 + 0.10×3 + 0.08×3 + 0.08×5 = 4.86. GQS raw = 0.40×7 + 0.20×6 + 0.15×4 + 0.15×4 + 0.10×3 = 5.50; persistent weak cash realization caps the final score at 5.00. The cap is not triggered simply because growth required inventory or because one year had heavy capex.

IAS = 0.25×4.86 + 0.35×1 + 0.20×2 + 0.10×2 + 0.10×3 = 2.465. Base IRR −3.11% less the fixed 15% equity hurdle gives a −18.09 percentage-point spread, hence R 1. GQS is Growth Quality, not governance quality. No factor is replaced by a neutral default or reweighted away.

L starts at 7 from the approximately 4.99-day 60-session lower-bound turnover test, then falls to 3 for the large discrete lot, repeated one-price declines, weaker recent turnover and missing live execution evidence. This is an explicit implementation downgrade, not a claim that BSE has prohibited trading. A reasonable one-point liquidity variation would move IAS by only 0.10 and would not alter the valuation conclusion.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The business traces to a 1997 proprietorship and was incorporated in 2006. It supplies non-tyre rubber and rubber-metal engineering products: railway rubber pads and sole plates, bridge bearings, expansion joints, vestibules, industrial sheets and other molded products. It sells into infrastructure, rail, industrial and commercial applications, rather than being a tyre producer or a recurring software-like business. Cemcon Rubber, previously a wholly owned subsidiary acquired in 2017, merged effective 1 April 2021 under a July 2022 regional-director order. This matters for older-period comparability.

The issuer describes a Kucharam manufacturing campus, approximately 60 tonnes daily installed capacity and a range of presses, testing capabilities and approvals. Website output claims vary around 30–38 tonnes daily; these are management descriptions, not independently audited utilization measurements. The prospectus explicitly warns that product mix, project timing and management assumptions limit capacity comparisons. No single tonne-to-revenue conversion is used to manufacture a precise market-share forecast.

The IPO earmarked ₹16.6896 crore for modernization/new conveyor-belt machinery, ₹5.95 crore for debt repayment, ₹3.4406 crore general purposes and ₹3.9198 crore issue expenses. The July 2026 Macroad licence adds an India-exclusive licensed-product opportunity for five years, with a USD 300,000 initial fee and 2.5% royalty on licensed-product net sales. It does not make all existing sales proprietary, and the model applies royalties only to an assumed licensed share.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Product qualification, application engineering, testing and delivery reliability can create entry friction in railway and structural components. A failure can be costly to the customer, so supplier approval is economically relevant. Nevertheless approved status does not establish monopoly pricing, guaranteed tender wins or permanently attractive returns. The prospectus itself describes competition on design, quality, price, delivery and relationships, and says there is no direct listed peer for its exact mix.

Freyssinet India’s primary product catalogue confirms competing elastomeric, pot and spherical bearings with integrated design, prototype testing and manufacturing. It is useful operating context, not a directly comparable quoted multiple. Broad tyre-company or unrelated rubber-product P/E ratios are not imported into the valuation. Conveyor-belt expansion also enters an existing competitive product category rather than an empty market.

FY 25 top-ten customers represented 50.11% of revenue, down from 53.93% in FY 24 and 64.63% in FY 23. That improvement is real, but concentration remains meaningful and the prospectus states there are no evergreen long-term customer commitments. Top-ten suppliers represented 77.80% of FY 25 raw-material purchases. The model therefore tests margins and working capital rather than treating order wins or supplier certifications as proof of a wide moat. MOAT 5 and DUR 6 distinguish useful technical capabilities from demonstrated durable pricing power.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Reviewed revenue observations are FY 21 ₹61.5831 crore, FY 22 ₹108.5053 crore, FY 23 ₹74.0848 crore, FY 24 ₹83.3384 crore, FY 25 ₹94.0518 crore and FY 26 ₹123.2499 crore. The first two are older statutory accounts with amalgamation-related scope; FY 23–25 are the IPO restated sequence and FY 26 the latest audited group statement. The US entity contributes no operating revenue. Annual reported additions are approximately +₹46.9223, −₹34.4205, +₹9.2536, +₹10.7134 and +₹29.1981 crore. The FY 23 decline must not disappear from the history.

Reported FY 21–26 CAGR is 14.89%, but the scored post-amalgamation FY 23–26 window is 18.49%, from ₹74.0848 to ₹123.2499 crore across three actual intervals. Five-year reported context is disclosed, not claimed to be a clean organic series. Ten-year comparable revenue and a verified price/volume decomposition were not established. REV 7 follows the 15–20% schedule without a further current-trajectory bonus.

FY 26 H 1 revenue was ₹42.7041 crore and H 2 ₹80.5458 crore. H 2 is the audited annual less unaudited H 1 balancing period, not a March quarter and not a comparable year-on-year growth test. October filings document ₹50.452 crore of rubber-pad orders over 24 months and ₹2.45145 crore over nine months. They support demand visibility but are gross award values, not a verified remaining backlog or incremental annual sales. Repeated secondary reports of a separate ₹13.41 crore order are not added twice or used to fabricate a backlog total.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The latest growth consumed substantial resources. FY 26 inventory was ₹51.2466 crore and receivables ₹22.6253 crore, together about 60% of annual revenue before other working-capital assets. CFO of about ₹1.6407 crore did not fund ₹29.4596 crore cash capex. Net IPO proceeds and additional borrowing funded the gap. This is a financing fact, not an allegation that inventory is fictitious. The test is whether collections, throughput and margins improve enough to earn returns on that capital.

Core FY 26 EBIT excludes ₹0.6861 crore other income and is about ₹14.3166 crore; normalized 25%-tax NOPAT is ₹10.7375 crore. An average equity-plus-debt less cash/investment proxy of roughly ₹85.37 crore gives approximately 12.58%, with IPO timing, earmarked cash and commissioning limiting precision. Incremental capital increased while operating NOPAT softened, so no durable excess-return conclusion is justified. CAP 4 reflects mixed economics, not an automatically negative score for investment.

The base model grows annual sales from ₹150 crore in FY 27 to a ₹280.53 crore FY 32 run rate. It includes 3.5% of sales recurring maintenance/growth capex, the remaining IPO machinery spend, existing capital advances/CWIP commissioning, royalties and licence renewal. Asset utilization and mix must improve as well; the model is not an engineering certification of capacity. Bull sales exceed ₹414 crore and require 4.5% capex intensity and better cash efficiency. These ambitious outcomes are scenarios, not achievements inferred from a machine purchase or licence signature.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The promoter family held approximately 67.30% at March 2026, with Mufaddal Deesawala and Sakina Deesawala the largest holders. The IPO diluted percentages by issuing 3,000,000 new shares rather than proving a promoter sale. Related transactions include remuneration, ₹0.354 crore rent to ABJ Rubber Metalico and an approximately ₹1.3422 crore ABJ receivable. FY 25 related sales of ₹4.1832 crore became zero in FY 26 while that balance persisted; collectability should be monitored. Director-family and COO compensation are disclosed, but disclosure alone is not a fairness opinion.

Tejaswini Kandra resigned as CFO effective 28 July 2026. A primary 29 August board filing appoints Kaushik Mehta effective that date; a website still naming the former CFO is stale, not proof the role remains vacant. Borrowing/security/investment authority increases up to ₹450 crore are shareholder/board powers, not lender commitments and not cash available for the model.

The final prospectus states that the former Nacharam facility lacked certain statutory approvals except its factory licence and was being used as a godown, with the old licence not surrendered. It also describes delayed foreign-subsidiary remittance and associated FEMA compliance risk. These are issuer-disclosed historical risks, not a new independent legal finding. No verified quantification of a new penalty or completed remedy was located; no arbitrary expected liability is invented. The annual audit is unmodified, but an unmodified opinion is not blanket legal-compliance clearance. GOV 5 and conditional G 1 preserve that distinction.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY 26 statutory PAT was ₹6.3393 crore versus ₹7.6839 crore, while EPS declined from ₹9.28 to ₹5.62 with dilution. The IPO restated FY 25 PAT is ₹8.0338 crore. Annexure V explicitly bridges original PAT through tax, depreciation and other adjustments; the difference is not an unexplained contradiction. Some prospectus management-discussion paragraphs repeat older amounts under a FY 25 heading. Signed statements and reconciliation tables take priority over that drafting, with no misconduct inference from boilerplate or rounding.

Cash realization is weak over several years: FY 23–26 CFO is ₹2.1563, −₹3.3554, ₹8.1081 and about ₹1.6407 crore, totaling ₹8.55 crore versus about ₹22.18 crore PAT on the disclosed restated/latest basis. Cash interest is classified in financing; subtracting it makes owner cash weaker, not stronger. FY 26 materials net inventory movement were ₹78.2801 crore, 63.51% of revenue, against 52.75% in FY 25. H 2 core EBITDA margin fell to 10.04%, versus 26.22% H 1, so the profit decline cannot be dismissed as IPO dilution alone. Receivables older than six months were ₹4.7241 crore, including ₹0.7452 crore older than three years, yet classified good.

Reported cash ₹5.4744 crore includes the ₹5 crore IPO reserve. The model spends ₹4.4282 crore on the matching remaining machinery allocation and up to ₹0.5718 crore on issue costs once. Financial-statement issue charges imply a lower ₹0.3996 crore remaining-cost bridge; that ₹0.1722 crore difference is tested, not treated as a material fraud finding. Separate tax assets ₹2.5601 crore and provision ₹2.1401 crore are excluded from ordinary working capital and netted conditionally, with an adverse no-credit case. Unprovided tax demands total ₹1.98 crore; GST appeal deposit ₹0.1215 crore is netted only in the settlement sensitivity. Bank guarantees are not automatically immediate cash losses. Audit KAMs on revenue, inventory and IPO use describe areas of audit focus, not qualifications.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹247.05 and 1.128 crore shares, equity value is about ₹278.67 crore, around 44 times FY 26 statutory PAT. The model uses an October 2031 terminal date, annual FY 27–31 cash bridges and a final fractional-year stub. It does not pretend the March balance sheet is an observed October cash balance. The unknown intervening period is modeled explicitly and checked against subsequent known commitments.

Base annual revenue is ₹150/180/207/231.84/255.024/280.5264 crore with 13% EBITDA before the licensed-product royalty. Operating working capital settles at 39% of annual sales. Licence fee is modeled at ₹95/USD, an explicit analyst FX assumption rather than asserted spot, and paid in FY 27; renewal is conservatively funded in the terminal stub. Licensed sales are 10% of revenue, so 2.5% royalty is not applied to the entire business. Debt costs 11.5% on opening balances adjusted for half-year repayments/new borrowing. Current term maturities are funded, subsequent amortization is estimated, and residual funding gaps issue hypothetical equity at a 30% price discount plus 5% fees. ₹450 crore authority is never treated as sanctioned funding.

Base terminal operating NOPAT is valued at an analyst 16 times, with 11 bear, 20 bull and 8 severe. Replacement depreciation and licence renewal are normalized; there is no zero-maintenance perpetuity. Base value ₹210.99 gives −3.11% IRR and roughly ₹104.90 entry for the 15% hurdle; gross equity required is ₹3.69 crore and cumulative debt draws/refinancing about ₹32.91 crore, not all incremental net debt. Bear ₹10.95 gives −46.38%, bull ₹617.20 gives 20.10%. Margin 16% still produces only about 5.87%; H 2-like 10% gives approximately −15.73%. Higher working capital, rates, tax-credit delay, tax settlement and extra capex are separately calculated in the linked model. The assumptions, not a transplanted peer multiple, drive the conclusion. Model correction, 20 October 2026: our earlier model omitted opening claims. The revised reference settles ₹0.1270000 crore at opening and deducts ₹0.0000000 crore of remaining net legacy employee obligations at terminal. These are corrections to our calculations, not changes to issuer-reported data. Future service expense remains funded through forecast margins. Accelerated settlement gives base return -3.1060% versus the reference -3.1060%. BQS, GQS, IAS and classification are unchanged. [S1]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
A credible adverse chain is slower order execution, raw-material pressure and weak collections, followed by debt refinancing at higher cost and equity issuance below the entry price. Bear revenue rises only slowly from ₹125 crore, margin is 9%, working capital 47% and the model includes ₹3 crore operating-asset impairment. It requires approximately ₹26.11 crore gross equity and yields ₹10.95 terminal value per diluted share. Severe assumptions produce zero modeled equity. A profitable income statement does not preclude that shareholder outcome.

Impairments are not fabricated cash payments. They reduce the recoverable opening working-capital stock, with future required working capital restored once through the cash-flow bridge; the loss also reduces accounting profit without a presumed tax shield. Unprovided tax demands are a separate explicitly hypothetical settlement case, not a second provision charged into every scenario. Existing capital advances and CWIP are commissioned without paying their historical cost again.

Liquidity can amplify permanent loss: a 1,200-share lot costs ₹296,460 at the dated close, so ₹5 lakh is not an exactly implementable whole-lot position. One lot is below and two lots ₹592,920 above the reference. The 60-session lower turnover-bound median suggests 12.47/4.99/2.49 trading days at 2%/5%/10% participation, before queue, spread and circuit effects. Twenty-session median is lower at ₹16.458 lakh, implying 6.08 days at 5%. Several recent sessions traded at a single declining price. That pattern does not prove a particular surveillance regime, but makes an orderly exit assumption unsafe.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold outcome from ₹247.05 means ₹1,235.25 per share and a tenfold outcome ₹2,470.50. Before any new dilution, these imply approximately ₹1,393.36 crore and ₹2,786.72 crore equity values. They are not established merely by doubling revenue, signing a technology licence or quoting a large addressable market. Debt, investment needs and the denominator all matter.

The reverse model holds base margins, working capital, capital intensity and valuation multiple fixed while solving revenue growth after FY 27. Meeting the 15% return hurdle requires approximately 44.77% annual growth after the ₹150 crore FY 27 base to a roughly ₹953.74 crore FY 32 run rate, with around ₹143.14 crore gross new equity under the financing convention. This is a mathematical expectation test, not a feasible capacity forecast. It demonstrates how dilution can consume enterprise growth.

The same fixed-economics search did not find a fivefold or tenfold per-share solution even within an extreme tested 0–90% annual-growth range. That is not proof such outcomes are impossible under every business model; it says this financed model does not support them. Materially stronger unit economics, lower working-capital intensity, much better entry price or less dilutive financing would have to be evidenced. The bull model produces only about 2.5 times entry value, already requiring substantial improvement. No multibagger designation is awarded.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
First, reconcile the next comparable half-year with the H 2 margin deterioration: revenue, material cost net inventory movement, EBITDA excluding other income, and PAT per share. A recovery above 13% operating margin must accompany actual collections, not merely a larger order announcement. Obtain a dated unexecuted order book and separate new awards, cancellations, execution and tax-inclusive contract values.

Second, track inventory and aged debtor realization, especially the ABJ balance and amounts older than a year. Require CFO after cash interest to improve and debt growth to moderate. Check IPO machinery commissioning, final utilization, the remaining issue-cost reconciliation and whether reported cash is still earmarked. Verify Macroad fee installments, licensed sales, royalties, renewal terms and measurable commercial output.

Third, monitor term-loan repayments, sanctioned undrawn facilities, actual borrowing costs and any proposed equity dilution. The model’s assumed debt capacity and discounted equity issuance are not commitments from financiers. Revisit the historical-premises and foreign-investment compliance disclosures when a specific remedy or liability is filed.

Before implementation, obtain current BSE restrictions, lot size, live depth and spread, and examine one-sided/circuit sessions. Refresh the reference-position test for the user’s actual proposed size rather than treating ₹5 lakh as a recommendation. Trigger reassessment for a material audit qualification, adverse balance correction, funding failure, customer cancellation, receivable write-off or substantive regulatory order. A share-price change alone does not resolve the cash-conversion problem.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: unattractive at the reviewed price under a conditional financed base case; watch for cash conversion and margin recovery, not a verified high-quality compounder or supported 5×/10× opportunity. BQS 4.86 and capped GQS 5.00 are business/growth-quality assessments; IAS 2.465 incorporates valuation, downside and execution at the dated ₹247.05 quote. These are research judgments with Medium evidence confidence, not certainty or personalized investment advice.

The low IAS is not caused by automatically excluding every BSE SME or by treating missing live spread as a critical financial hold. A numerical conditional implementation score is supported by the complete dated secondary sample and verified lot, then conservatively adjusted for actual one-price behavior and size constraints. Nor is the conclusion a governance accusation: issuer-disclosed risks and ordinary restatements are kept distinct from proven wrongdoing.

A materially lower price could improve expected return, but the approximate ₹104.90 hurdle entry is model-dependent and not an executable limit-order instruction. Better margins without better cash conversion can still require dilution. Conversely, demonstrated recovery in cash return, reduced working capital and non-dilutive funding could improve the business assessment. No automatic purchase or sale action follows from this dossier.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary evidence comprises the FY 26 audited annual report and May 30 results, final IPO prospectus, signed restated financials and reconciliation, FY 22 signed accounts with FY 21 comparator, IPO-utilisation statement, July technology licence, August CFO appointment, and October railway order filings. The two October PDFs are issuer documents obtained through a Business Standard mirror, with BSE document identifiers retained. Security identity/lot/capital come from the official interoperability master. Daily BSE price/volume observations are secondary EquityPandit data, explicitly not official turnover or guaranteed execution. Freyssinet’s primary catalogue is used only for operating competition.

Important remaining gaps are a current verified remaining order book, independent customer collections, exact future capacity/maintenance engineering, lender commitments for modeled refinancing, complete current BSE restrictions/live depth, and a documented remedy or quantified liability for the historical compliance disclosures. These limit forecasts and monitoring; they do not make the reviewed aggregate audited numbers unusable. The tax-asset netting and issue-cost difference have explicit bounded sensitivities. No undisclosed expected penalty is inserted to manufacture a score.

Forecast growth, margins, working-capital ratios, FX 90/95/105/110, financing rates/caps, equity discounts/fees and terminal multiples are analyst assumptions, not management guidance or market facts. They are visible in the linked annual model, including every debt draw, repayment, cash-tax use and share issuance. The model is reproducible and the score audit is separate from narrative.

valuation.status: Conditional financed annual scenarios; analyst estimates, not approved funding

hurdle.assumption: Base margins, working capital, capex intensity and multiple; does not establish physical capacity for this revenue.

fivefold.assumption: Base margins, working capital, capex intensity and multiple; does not establish physical capacity for this revenue.

tenfold.assumption: Base margins, working capital, capex intensity and multiple; does not establish physical capacity for this revenue.

assumption_basis: Base revenue is ₹150, ₹180, ₹207, ₹231.84, ₹255.024 and ₹280.5264 crore for FY 27 through the FY 32 annual run rate. Growth is an analyst scenario informed by historical sales and documented orders, not a verified remaining backlog.

Base EBITDA margin is 13% before the licensed-product royalty, a partial recovery from H 2 FY 26 core margin of approximately 10.04%, below full-year 15.65%. Bear 9%, bull 15% then 17% and severe 8% are explicit alternatives. The former 15.5–16% draft base was superseded after the latest-half review.

Opening ordinary working capital includes inventory, receivables, supplier/staff/GST advances, prepaid costs, other operating advances and security deposits, less trade/operating liabilities and gratuity. Income-tax balances, GST appeal deposit and capital advances are separated. Impairments reduce opening recoverable working capital and are funded once through the closing requirement, not as a separate fictitious cash payment.

Cash ₹5.4744 crore plus liquid mutual funds ₹0.4999 crore is available subject to authorized use; ₹1 crore operating reserve is retained outside distributable cash. The ₹5 crore IPO reserve funds matching ₹4.4282 crore machinery and up to ₹0.5718 crore issue-cost outflows once. It is not removed and then financed again. Lower remaining issue cost ₹0.3996 crore is separately tested.

Existing capital advances ₹0.8453 crore and CWIP ₹5.0109 crore are commissioned without repaying their historical cost. Recurring maintenance/growth capex is 3.5% of base sales, 3% bear, 4.5% bull and 2.5% severe, additional to remaining IPO machinery. Terminal depreciation is at least recurring capex rather than a zero-replacement perpetuity. These are analytical estimates, not an engineering study.

Macroad initial fee USD 300000 uses explicit scenario FX assumptions of ₹95/USD base, 105 bear, 90 bull and 110 severe. Full fee is conservatively funded in FY 27 despite phased contractual payment; a further renewal fee is funded in the terminal stub. Five-year amortization and normalized terminal renewal cost prevent treating the licence as perpetual free technology. No renewal agreement is asserted.

Royalty is 2.5% of licensed-product net sales, not all revenue. Licensed share is 10% base/bear, 20% bull and 5% severe. EBITDA assumptions are before this explicit deduction, avoiding double charging an already net margin.

Base debt interest is 11.5% on opening debt less half-year scheduled repayment plus half-year new draws, solved iteratively. FY 27 term principal ₹7.6212 crore follows current maturities; later remaining term balance is amortized using an explicit analytical schedule. Refinancing is separately visible, not mistaken for all-new net borrowing.

Analytical debt limits are scenario ceilings, constrained by EBITDA while allowing existing balance refinancing. They are not sanctioned availability. Funding gaps require equity at 30% below entry with 5% fees. New debt, mandatory repayment, surplus repayment, equity and dilution appear annually. No ₹450 crore board authority is treated as cash.

Current tax assets ₹2.5601 crore offset the ₹2.1401 crore provision conditionally; only the ₹0.4200 crore residual credit reduces subsequent modeled cash tax. Ordinary working capital excludes both. A no-credit case instead pays the provision and grants no asset collection. Separate unprovided tax-demand settlement nets only the ₹0.1215 crore GST appeal deposit; it is not mechanically added to every scenario.

Tax is 25% of positive pre-impairment profit, without an assumed loss tax shield. Terminal operating NOPAT multiples are 16 base, 11 bear, 20 bull and 8 severe. No listed peer multiple is transplanted; dividends are zero. Exact terminal date 19 October 2031 uses a fractional FY 32 stub.

The opening March 2026 balance sheet is not claimed to be October observed cash. The FY 27 bridge covers known and estimated intervening movements. Reverse growth equations are feasibility diagnostics only; extremely high implied sales do not establish capacity.

Opening current claims settle once. Remaining net noncurrent legacy employee obligations are deducted from terminal equity, not assigned an invented legal maturity. Future employee service expense is assumed cash-funded through forecast operating margins; it is not added back. The terminal deduction covers only the legacy balance not otherwise paid. Accelerated settlement is a timing sensitivity, not a predicted exit schedule. FY26 note10: accrued interest but not due ₹12.70 lakh removed from WC, now settled once. Both gratuity maturities already remain in WC.
